Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3–3.5-month history of poor appetite, low energy, low mood  
  • Episodic palpitations and subjective dyspnea, especially in elevators; no exertional dyspnea when able to walk a mile (patient currently sedentary)  
  • Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone (~14 lb) over ~6 months  
  • Intermittent nausea without vomiting; normal bowel motions, no diarrhea, blood, or mucus  
  • Occasional headaches, nausea at work  
  • History of hypothyroidism; patient stopped thyroxine “since I changed doctor” (timeframe unclear)  
- Relevant family medical history: Not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  
  • Thyroxine (levothyroxine) – ceased; dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • No current medications or OTC products reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Married; reports decreased libido/“nightly activities” at partner’s request. No further sexual history.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Currently not walking/exercising; diminished appetite and low oral intake.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: Not recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Describes feeling “down”; reluctant to label as depression. No suicidal thoughts disclosed.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Married; works as a lawyer; reports some work-related stress; no caring duties noted.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Planned: “General set of bloods” (CBC for anemia, U&E, LFT, thyroid profile, vitamin levels).  
- No other investigations ordered at this consult.  
- Cervical screening, STI screen, mammogram: Not applicable/not discussed.  
- Other pathology: To be determined once initial blood results returned.  

Management Plan

- Arrange pathology form and support line referral for comprehensive blood tests (CBC, renal, liver, thyroid, vitamins, ±lipids, fasting glucose).  
- Advise patient to seek urgent care (ED) if chest pain, worsening palpitations, or new bowel changes occur.  
- Plan follow-up appointment once blood results available; possible physical examination at that time.  
- Reinforced contacting service via app’s 0300 number for any concerns before results return.  
- Education: Explained importance of results to guide next steps; no immediate change to medication pending labs (consider restarting thyroxine if indicated).  

Consider (not yet actioned):  
• Mental health assessment/support if low mood persists  
• Lifestyle counseling (nutrition, graded exercise) once underlying causes clarified  
• CTG registration, preventive immunizations review at future visit  

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs (BP, HR), weight/BMI, smoking/alcohol history, immunization review, depression screening, cardiovascular risk factors, oral/vision/hearing assessments.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient reports hypothyroidism but experiencing symptoms more consistent with hyperthyroid/palpitations (noted by clinician). Weight-loss timeline somewhat unclear (3 vs 6 months).  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional inaudible/overlapping speech but main clinical details intelligible.
